explain.say: The excited dye releases the energy as light, with almost no heat. This is chemiluminescence. Cold slows the reaction, so a glow stick in the freezer glows dimmer but lasts longer.

faq.q: What chemicals are inside a glow stick?
faq.a: Hydrogen peroxide in a small glass vial, and around it an oxalate ester chemical with a fluorescent dye dissolved in it.
asks: What is the liquid in a glow stick?

faq.q: What decides a glow stick's colour?
faq.a: The dye. The reaction makes the same energy each time, and different dyes turn it into different colours of light.
asks: Why are glow sticks different colours?

faq.q: Why do glow sticks last longer in the freezer?
faq.a: Cold slows the chemical reaction down, so the glow is dimmer but the chemicals are used up more slowly. Warmth makes it brighter but shorter.
asks: Does freezing a glow stick make it last?

faq.a: It is light made by a chemical reaction rather than by heat. When living things do it, like fireflies, it is called bioluminescence.
asks: How can light be made without heat?

faq.a: The chemicals can irritate skin and eyes, so never cut one open. If the liquid leaks, wash it off with water.

facts: Light from a chemical reaction is called chemiluminescence; when living things such as fireflies make it, it is called bioluminescence.
In warm water a glow stick shines brighter but runs out sooner.

quiz.say: Why does a glow stick last longer in the freezer?
quiz.show: Why does a glow stick last longer in the freezer?
quiz.why: A slower reaction uses the chemicals up more slowly, so the glow is dimmer but longer lasting.

wrong.0: Light cannot be stored as ice; the chemicals simply react more slowly.
wrong.2: The amount of dye stays the same; only the reaction speed changes.
